---
title: "Get started in Stata"
---

This page runs a first analysis of the example data with the Stata command.
The [R version](apexog.html) runs the same analysis on the same file. The
output below comes from apexog 0.21.2 in StataNow 19.5
(`data-raw/site_examples.do` in the R package's repository).

## Install

```stata
net install apexog, from("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jespernwulff/stata-apexog/main/")
help apexog
```

apexog requires Stata 18 or later. It fits the control-function probit itself
(`regress`, `probit`, `fracreg`, `poisson` or `biprobit`, plus Mata) and does
not need StataNow's `cfprobit`.

## The data and the question

```stata
use "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jespernwulff/apexog/main/inst/extdata/promotion.dta", clear
describe
```

The data are simulated. The outcome `promoted` is binary. Hours of `training`
are endogenous: employees choose training partly on an unobserved ability that
also drives promotion. A training `subsidy` shifts training and serves as the
instrument; `tenure` and `manager` are controls; `team` identifies 200 teams.

The subsidy is only plausibly excluded: it might affect promotion directly. apexog
asks how much such a direct effect, *γ*, would change the average partial
effect (APE) of training on the probability of promotion.

## A range for the violation: `uci`

The syntax follows `ivregress` and `cfprobit`: outcome, controls, and the
endogenous regressor with its instrument in parentheses. Here the subsidy's
direct effect is assumed to lie between −0.10 and 0.10 on the latent index:

```stata
apexog uci promoted tenure manager (training = subsidy), gmin(-0.10) gmax(0.10) grid(11)
```

```{.stata-output}
Running UCI grid: 11 point(s) per instrument, 1 instrument(s), 11 total grid point(s).

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Plausibly-exogenous APE bounds (CHR 2012, UCI method)
Estimator: cfprobit  |  First stage: linear  |  SE: two-step  |  N = 4000
Endogenous: training
Target:    APE of every endogenous regressor (default)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Baseline (gamma = 0):
    APE(training)              =  0.144457  (SE 0.008376)  [ 0.128040,  0.160874]

Scale:     1 latent-index unit of gamma = 0.2091 pr. points per unit of Z (avg., baseline)
           1 structural-latent unit of gamma = 1.1986 latent-index units  (sigma_tilde = 0.8343)

UCI union over gamma grid (11 point(s) per IV):
    gamma_subsidy range  : [-0.1000,  0.1000]   exact Pr scale: [-0.0209,  0.0209]

    APE(training) bounds       = [ 0.097095,  0.190449]
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

- **Baseline**: the APE with a valid instrument (*γ* = 0). It equals
  `cfprobit promoted tenure manager (training = subsidy)` followed by
  `margins, dydx(training)`, point estimate and standard error. The standard
  error is the Murphy–Topel two-step standard error.
- **Scale**: one unit of *γ* on the latent index changes the probability of
  promotion by 0.209 per unit of the subsidy, on average. See
  [Which scale for the violation?](gamma-scale.html).
- **UCI union**: the union of the 95% confidence intervals over the eleven
  values of *γ*. For any violation in the range the APE lies between 0.097 and
  0.190.

apexog is an estimation command. `e(b)` and `e(V)` hold the baseline estimate
and its variance, so `lincom`, `test` and `estimates store` work; the bounds are
in `e(lb_training)` and `e(ub_training)`, the grid in `e(grid)`:

```stata
lincom training
```

```{.stata-output}
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    promoted | Coefficient  Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [95% conf. interval]
-------------+----------------------------------------------------------------
         (1) |   .1444568   .0083227    17.36   0.000     .1281446     .160769
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

With `graph`, apexog plots the estimate and its confidence band against the
assumed violation. Over ±0.20 the lower bound still stays above zero:

```stata
apexog uci promoted tenure manager (training = subsidy), gmin(-0.20) gmax(0.20) grid(21) graph
```

![UCI graph from Stata: APE of training and its 95% confidence band against the assumed violation](../reference/figures/stata-uci.png){width=90%}

## A prior for the violation: `ltz`

Instead of a hard range you can give a prior. Here *γ* is normal with mean 0
and variance 0.0025:

```stata
apexog ltz promoted tenure manager (training = subsidy), mu(0) omega(0.0025) iterations(1000) seed(101)
```

```{.stata-output}
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Plausibly-exogenous APE bounds (CHR 2012, LTZ method, gaussian prior)
Estimator: cfprobit  |  First stage: linear  |  SE: two-step  |  N = 4000
Endogenous: training
Target:    APE of every endogenous regressor (default)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Baseline (gamma = 0):
    APE(training)              =  0.144457  (SE 0.008376)

Scale:     1 latent-index unit of gamma = 0.2091 pr. points per unit of Z (avg., baseline)
           1 structural-latent unit of gamma = 1.1986 latent-index units  (sigma_tilde = 0.8343)

LTZ prior:
    gamma_subsidy ~ N( 0.0000,  0.0025)
      exact Pr scale of the draws: mean  0.0002, sd  0.0101
    iterations         = 1000

LTZ 95% intervals (sampling noise convolved with prior; CHR 2012 eq. 7):
    APE(training) 95% CI = [ 0.109099,  0.176167]

Prior-only spread of the point APEs (sensitivity band, no sampling noise):
    APE(training) 95% range = [ 0.114937,  0.174157]
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

apexog draws *γ* 1,000 times, refits at every draw, and adds each refit's
sampling noise to its estimate. The **95% CI** accounts for both the
uncertainty about *γ* and the sampling uncertainty; the **prior-only range**
shows how far the point estimate moves across the prior alone. The draws are
in `e(gamma_sim)`, the refit estimates in `e(ape_sim)` and the combined draws
in `e(ape_sim_cnv)`.

## The violation in probability points

With `gunits(pr)` every value of *γ* is read as a change in the probability of
the outcome per unit of the instrument. A direct effect of at most 2 percentage
points:

```stata
apexog uci promoted tenure manager (training = subsidy), gunits(pr) gmin(-0.02) gmax(0.02) grid(11)
```

```{.stata-output}
Scale:     1 latent-index unit of gamma = 0.2091 pr. points per unit of Z (avg., baseline)
           1 structural-latent unit of gamma = 1.1986 latent-index units  (sigma_tilde = 0.8343)
           gunits(pr): user gamma values were probability points; divided by m_phi.  Values below are latent units.
           (first order; exact Pr-scale equivalents shown alongside)

UCI union over gamma grid (11 point(s) per IV):
    gamma_subsidy range  : [-0.0957,  0.0957]   exact Pr scale: [-0.0200,  0.0200]

    APE(training) bounds       = [ 0.098438,  0.189164]
```

## Clustered standard errors

```stata
apexog uci promoted tenure manager (training = subsidy), gmin(-0.10) gmax(0.10) grid(11) vce(cluster team)
```

```{.stata-output}
Baseline (gamma = 0):
    APE(training)              =  0.144457  (SE 0.007403)  [ 0.129948,  0.158966]
...
    APE(training) bounds       = [ 0.099118,  0.188665]
```
